D.t: Amanda Janoo trails by 7.4 and wins 12% of simulations. Closing it takes about 12,115 voters switching sides, or 24,231 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +15.4 and D +0.9. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +2.4. Your best recent poll is University of New Hampshire at D +6.3; your worst is Braun Research at R +9.3. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Chittenden, a projected net 6,834 votes; Windham, a projected net 5,027 votes; Washington, a projected net 908 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Chittenden, D +7.7, 26.9% of the vote; Washington, D +2.9, 9.6% of the vote; Windsor, R +2.9, 9.3% of the vote; Addison, R +5.3, 6.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Amanda Janoo runs furthest behind in Grand Isle, Chittenden, Lamoille. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 93% of voters, 41 to 56, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.64 points; Small counties, 73% of voters, 40 to 56, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.65 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 72% of voters, 48 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.58 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Amanda Janoo: 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 20 to 75, Immigration voters 24 to 69, 2022 voters who skipped 2024 31 to 61. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$307K cash against $202K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 1.1 points toward Amanda Janoo. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $400K helping Phil Scott and $40K helping Amanda Janoo.

R.t: Phil Scott leads by 7.4 in the forecast and wins 88% of simulations. The cushion is about 24,231 votes; a one point swing is about 1,646 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +0.9 and R +15.4. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +2.4. Your best recent poll is Braun Research at R +9.3; your worst is University of New Hampshire at D +6.3. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Rutland, a projected net 10,224 votes; Franklin, a projected net 8,909 votes; Orleans, a projected net 4,202 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Chittenden, D +7.7, 26.9% of the vote; Washington, D +2.9, 9.6% of the vote; Windsor, R +2.9, 9.3% of the vote; Addison, R +5.3, 6.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Phil Scott runs furthest behind in Windham, Bennington, Orleans. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 93% of voters, 56 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.64 points; Small counties, 73% of voters, 56 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.65 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 72% of voters, 45 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.58 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Phil Scott: Asian and other voters 26 to 71, Health care and Social Security voters 34 to 59, Corruption voters 39 to 54. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$202K cash against $307K. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

R.h: What the ballots so far say
R.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 1.1 points away from Phil Scott. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
